label: Applied neo-Kantian methodological distinctions between natural sciences and cultural understanding
description: Max Weber adopted Immanuel Kant's insights and systematically extended them into new metaphysical, ethical, or epistemological domains.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Immanuel Kant's perspective to Max Weber's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Inter-epochal reception: transmitting insights from the German Idealism & Romanticism across history into the 20th Century Phenomenon & Analysis.

label: Contested Marx's materialist determinism by demonstrating how religious ideas drive capitalist development
description: Max Weber engaged in a direct critique of Karl Marx's foundational principles, rejecting core axioms in favor of a dialectically opposed framework.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Karl Marx's perspective to Max Weber's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Inter-epochal reception: transmitting insights from the 19th Century Divergences across history into the 20th Century Phenomenon & Analysis.

label: Nietzschean critique of asceticism and modern disenchantment deeply shaped Weberian rationalization
description: Max Weber was fundamentally influenced by Friedrich Nietzsche's central inquiries, which shaped the evolution of their philosophical worldview.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Friedrich Nietzsche's perspective to Max Weber's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Inter-epochal reception: transmitting insights from the 19th Century Divergences across history into the 20th Century Phenomenon & Analysis.

label: Articulated how bureaucratic rationalization imprisons modern society in an iron cage
description: Max Weber formulated and introduced the concept of "The Iron Cage of Rationality", which became a seminal contribution in social-theory philosophy.
dialecticalTension: Formulating an epistemic apparatus to resolve central problems in social-theory.
historicalContext: Introduced during the 20th Century Phenomenon & Analysis as part of Max Weber's canonical writings.

label: Weberian instrumental rationality merged with Marxist critique in Dialectic of Enlightenment
description: Theodor W. Adorno was fundamentally influenced by Max Weber's central inquiries, which shaped the evolution of their philosophical worldview.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Max Weber's perspective to Theodor W. Adorno's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Direct contemporaneous dialogue and pedagogical transmission during the 20th Century Phenomenon & Analysis era.

label: Habermas reconstructed Weberian rationalization theory in Theory of Communicative Action
description: Jürgen Habermas adopted Max Weber's insights and systematically extended them into new metaphysical, ethical, or epistemological domains.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Max Weber's perspective to Jürgen Habermas's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Inter-epochal reception: transmitting insights from the 20th Century Phenomenon & Analysis across history into the Contemporary & Post-Structural.
